notes: PrefLib file 00020-00000001.toi (dataset 00020, 'pierce'). Counting rule, as far as we know: Instant runoff, single-winner. 64 ballots with two or more candidates tied at one rank were left out (not counted as blank). A 'Write-In' candidate stands for all write-in votes combined.

label_sources.official_winners: Pierce County "Ranked Choice Voting Results Table, Contest: Pierce County Auditor" (https://piercecountywa.gov/DocumentCenter/View/6991/summary), read through search-engine extracts because the county site blocks automated access; Tacoma Daily Index, "Anderson sworn in as Pierce County Auditor".
label_sources.max_ranks: Pierce County used a 3-rank ballot for its 2008 and 2009 ranked-choice races (county sample ballot; every ballot in the file has 3 or fewer ranks).

label_notes: Special election for the one year left in the term. All three candidates appeared as nonpartisan, so parties is null.
